observations: Signs with a user-provided keybox; a keybox is not included.
Harvests the existing device root-of-trust values; those values are not profile-configurable.
The current emulator provides software, unlocked and unverified values.
Provides Windows TPM-backed cryptographic primitives as a separate host process.
The inspected attestation record reports TrustedEnvironment but obtains its default signing key and chain from the software attestation certificate helpers.
That default does not supply a provisioned manufacturer identity; TPM-backed storage and Android manufacturer certification are separate requirements.

candidates.project: Android AVF protected VM remote attestation
observations: Requires a UDS-rooted DICE public key registered with the RKP factory/backend.
Attests a protected VM payload using a distinct certificate extension; it is not an Android physical-handset identity.
Moving to a VM implementation alone does not provide the missing registered device identity.

host_readonly_observations.tpm_state: not established; Get-Tpm returned no usable Boolean status
host_readonly_observations.note: CIM virtualization fields under an active hypervisor are not used to conclude that CPU virtualization is disabled.

conclusion: The measured emulator has no established manufacturer-backed Android attestation identity. None of the reviewed projects supplies that identity merely by installing its code. CPU topology and stability changes do not resolve this cryptographic requirement.

observations: Factory is a fallback label when neither the Google-root check nor AOSP certificate-name heuristics match.
The Duck public-key fingerprint equals the independent root SubjectPublicKeyInfo fingerprint; the differing certificate fingerprint is expected.
The six Bootloader danger entries reuse four signed boot fields. CPU allocation does not alter those fields.
The interface describes a DICE chain originating from a unique-device-secret key; production device identity is separate from implementing the API.
Version 3, associated with Android 14, removes the older testMode request mechanism. Older test-mode documentation is not evidence of this guest backend behavior.
The unregistered test-CA subject alone is not used to infer the provisioning server policy. The measured signed software level and nonmatching external roots remain the evidence.
